TARGETED renderer/tokenization overhead improvement discovered while investigating #41390.

## Problem

For short batched offline embedding workloads, `LLM.embed` can spend avoidable time in renderer-side tokenization before requests reach the engine. In the Nemotron embedding repro from #41390, `BaseRenderer.tokenize_prompts` tokenized each simple text prompt with one `tokenizer.encode(...)` call even when the tokenizer supported list/batch tokenization.

This does not explain the entire vLLM vs. Transformers gap. It is a localized vLLM-side overhead in the steady-state renderer/tokenization path for batched text embedding requests.

## Root Cause

## Purpose
The FP4 MoE Marlin prep functions repack each expert's weight into a Python list and torch.cat the list into the final [E, ...] tensor. title: [Slop][Kernel] Skip non-local Marlin ReLU2 activations
body:
Marlin stores its first MoE GEMM output as `[num_tokens * top_k, intermediate_size]`.

With expert parallelism, Marlin excludes routes owned by other ranks from both GEMMs using
`expert_map`. `apply_moe_activation()` still applies ReLU2 to every row of the intermediate
buffer, including remote routes which the second GEMM will never consume. With TP2, roughly
half of this activation work is unused.

This PR adds a routed ReLU2 Triton kernel. Each program handles one token, loops over its
top-k experts, and computes `max(x, 0)²` only when expert_map identifies the route as local.
Remote rows remain untouched; the following Marlin GEMM and MoE reduction already ignore
those same rows.

The existing activation path remains unchanged when routing metadata is not supplied.
